story: Heitsi-eibib is a mythic hero and trickster figure in Khoikhoi mythology, associated with Gaunab and Tsui'goab. He is a shapeshifter, sometimes appearing as an adult, sometimes as a child. In one story, the child Heitsi-eibib became an adult and had sexual intercourse with his mother, then suddenly turned into a baby again. He is repeatedly resurrected and engages in deceptive and immoral acts, and these transgressions represent deeper cultural lessons. He has many real tombs in the form of cairns located in South Africa and Namibia. He is also associated with celestial bodies, including the sun and moon. One of his notable deeds involves defeating Ga-Gorib, a monster associated with Gaunab, the god of the underworld. Ga-Gorib would sit at the edge of a deep hole and challenge people to throw a stone at his forehead; if anyone accepted, the stone would bounce back and kill the thrower. Heitsi-eibib discovered these deaths and decided to defeat Ga-Gorib. He went to Ga-Gorib's location, where Ga-Gorib challenged him to throw a stone at his forehead. Heitsi-eibib refused the challenge, distracted Ga-Gorib, and struck him behind the ear instead. Ga-Gorib lost his balance and fell into the deep hole, dying. In another version, Ga-Gorib chased Heitsi-eibib after he refused the challenge; they fought and both fell into the pit, but only Ga-Gorib died, while Heitsi-eibib survived.
